chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān, raising it from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), said:
They suck at the scant water and leave the mighty river.

It was said to him: What is the mighty river? He said: The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and the knowledge that Allah gave him. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gathered for Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله) the sunnahs of the Prophets, from Ādam onward in succession up to Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله).

It was said to him: And what are those sunnahs? He said: The knowledge of the Prophets in its entirety. And indeed, the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) placed all of that with Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام).

Then a man said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah, is Amīr al-Muʾminīn more knowledgeable, or some of the Prophets? So Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) said: Listen to what he is saying! Indeed, Allah opens the hearing of whomsoever He wills. I told him that Allah gathered for Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله) the knowledge of the Prophets, and that he gathered all of that with Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام), and yet he asks me: Is he more knowledgeable, or some of the Prophets?

key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the Commander of the Faithful, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (عليه السلام)
key_terms.الثِّمَادَ: scant or stagnant water; used here as a metaphor for lesser sources people cling to
key_terms.النَّهَرَ الْعَظِيمَ: the mighty river; a metaphor for the Messenger of Allah and his divinely granted knowledge
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah, Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله)
key_terms.سُنَنَ النَّبِيِّينَ: the prophetic traditions and inherited ways of all the Prophets
key_terms.عِلْمُ النَّبِيِّينَ: the knowledge possessed by the Prophets in its entirety
key_terms.مَسَامِعَ: hearings or faculties of hearing; indicating divine enabling to understand

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the knowledge inherited by the Imams from the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله)?
ai.summary: This hadith presents the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) as the vast source of divinely granted knowledge, in contrast to lesser sources people may cling to. It states that the knowledge and sunnah of the Prophets were gathered in Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله) and then entrusted to Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام), highlighting the transmitted authority of the Ahl al-Bayt in Shia thought.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Ali Bin Al Numan, 
raising it from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said: ‘
Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They (people) are sucking the moisture and are leaving the magnificent river’.

It was said to himasws, ‘And what is the magnificent river?’ Hesaww said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww and the Knowledge which Allahazwj Granted himsaww. Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Gathered for Muhammadsaww, the Sunnah of the Prophetsas, from Adamas and brought forwards flowing up to Muhammadsaww’.
It was said to himasws, ‘And what is that Sunnah?’ Heasws said: ‘Knowledge of the Prophetsas in its entirety, and that Rasool-Allahsaww rendered that, all of it with Amir Al-Momineenasws’.

So a man said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘O son<sup>asws</sup> of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! So, is Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> more knowledgeable or some of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>?’ So Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Listen to what he is saying! Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Opens the hearing of the ones He<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires to. I<sup>asws</sup> narrated to him that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Gathered to Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> the Knowledge of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>, and that he<sup>saww</sup> gathered that, all of it, to be with Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>, and he is asking me<sup>asws</sup>, is he<sup>asws</sup> more knowledgeable or some of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>?’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad from Ali ibn Nu‘man, in a marfu’ manner (rafa’ahu) from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following.
“They try to absorb the little moisture but ignore the huge river.”

Someone asked him, “What is (this) huge river?” The Imams (a.s.)said, “It is the Messenger of Allah (s.a.) and the Knowledge that Allah gave to him. Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, combined in Muhammad (s.a.) the Sunnah (traditions) of the all the prophets from Adam onwards to Muhammad (s.a.).”

Someone asked him, “What are those sunnah (traditions)?” The Imams (a.s.) said, “They are all the knowledge of the prophets (s.a.). The Messenger of Allah transferred all of them to Amir al-Mu’minin Ali (a.s.).”

The man then said, “O son of the Messenger of Allah, is Amir al-Mu’minin Ali (a.s.) more knowledgeable or some of the prophets?” Abu Ja‘far (a.s.) replied, “Listen, everyone to what he just said. Allah opens the ears of whoever He wants. I said to him that Allah combined for Muhammad (s.a.) the knowledge of the prophets and he combined all of it with Amir al-Mu’minin Ali (a.s.). He now asks me, “Was he (Ali (a.s.) more knowledgeable or some of the prophets?”
